From today's featured article
Misti as seen from Arequipa
Misti
is a volcano in the southern Peruvian
Andes
, rising above
Arequipa
, Peru's second-largest city. Because it is only 12
km (8
mi) from Arequipa and its million-plus inhabitants, it is considered one of the world's most dangerous volcanoes. Narrow valleys on its western and southern flanks pose particular threats, as
mudflows
and
fast-moving flows of hot volcanic debris
could be channelled into the urban area and into important infrastructure, like
hydropower plants
. The last two significant eruptions were 2,000 years ago and from 1440 to 1470. Even a moderate eruption could deposit
volcanic ash
and
tephra
over most of the city. A
volcano observatory
monitors the mountain. The
Inca
viewed the volcano as a threat, and during the 1440–1470 eruption offered
human sacrifices
(
capacocha
) on Misti and neighbouring mountains to placate the volcano. The
mummies
on Misti form the largest known Inca human sacrifi
